policy: A question is VERIFIED_PYQ only after its exact wording, options, exam/year/paper, and official answer are checked against authoritative evidence. An official portal URL alone is not per-question verification.

papers.notes: A regression test screens 30 distinctive short fragments anchored to questions in this official paper against all six static bank collections: seed, expanded, CSAT, mapped question bank, priority bank, and catalog bank. Exact normalized phrase matches are asserted to be zero. Conservative fuzzy lexical candidates are printed for manual review; their count is a triage signal only. This is not a full semantic paper-to-bank match or item-level answer-key verification. No item was promoted to VERIFIED_PYQ.

sources.answer_key_archive_notes: UPSC's official 2026 provisional keys for GS-I and CSAT were retrieved visually and show set-wise answers; GS-I records one dropped question (99 scored) and CSAT records no dropped questions (80 scored). The 2025 GS-I official final-key link was resolved from the official-key link on a secondary index page to the UPSC domain, but the PDF itself timed out in this retrieval run. The official paper PDFs for 2025/2026 were too large for the current text-retrieval path. No question has been checked end-to-end against both exact official paper text/options and official answer evidence. The 2026 keys are provisional. The 2023 key remains unresolved.

sources.notes: SSC's official 9 January 2026 notice confirms that CGL 2025 Tier-I final answer keys and candidate response sheets were login-accessible from 09.01.2026 18:00 to 08.02.2026 18:00 and would not remain available afterward. The official 16 October 2025 tentative-key notice states that question and option sequence in the challenge module may differ from each candidate's actual examination order; the candidate's response sheet is needed to map exact shift/order. The access window has expired, and no candidate response sheet or public shift paper was retrieved. No static-bank item was matched to an exact shift/stem/options/final answer.
sources.official_2023_tier1_tentative_answer_key: Official notice states CGL Tier-I 2023 was held 14–27 July 2023 and candidate response sheets/tentative answer keys were login-accessible 1–4 August 2023, after which response sheets would not remain available. This confirms historical access limitations, not item-level matches.

sources.notes: RBI's official Call Letters page and 2025/2026 Grade B Phase-I handout pages were checked. They establish the examination date, instructions and format, but are not actual past question papers or official answer keys. No public item-level question-paper/answer-key source was established for RBI Grade B Phase-I. Sample items in a handout must not be relabelled as PYQs. No item was promoted to VERIFIED_PYQ.

paper_coverage_check.paper: UPSC CSE Prelims 2023 GS Paper I, Test Booklet Series A
paper_coverage_check.method: Case-insensitive literal term search across six static source-code bank/build files: data/priority_question_bank.js, data/seed_questions.js, data/expanded_question_bank.js, data/csat_questions.js, data/catalog_question_bank.js, data/question_bank.js.
paper_coverage_check.interpretation: None of the 30 literal topic terms probed was found in these six static bank/build files. This is a narrow coverage-gap check, not proof that every related concept is absent and not a substitute for exact stem/options/answer verification. These official-paper questions should be considered candidates for new provenance-backed records only after answer-key verification; do not label existing similar concepts as PYQs.

ssc_next_step: Use the official 2023 Tier-I final-answer-key listing as the next accessible source target; extract actual item-level records only if the official linked response-sheet/question-paper content can be retrieved and tied to a shift and answer.
